discoveries.headline: Crypto and your tax, in three minutes
discoveries.why: The Australian Taxation Office's plain guide: what counts as a crypto asset, why there are no special tax rules, and why staking rewards count as income. Worth knowing before you buy, not after.

discoveries.headline: Inside COP31: the promises, and who pays
discoveries.why: The Earth Negotiations Bulletin team on the first days in Antalya: a push to move faster away from fossil fuels, the start of the second global stocktake, and a $5.1 billion hole in climate finance. The clearest picture of where the talks really stand.

discoveries.headline: A ghostly sawfish wins Australia's top nature photo prize
discoveries.why: Matt Deakin's drone caught a critically endangered green sawfish gliding out of the mist in the Pilbara, a turtle beside it. Some people asked if it was AI. It isn't: it's what's still out there, worth protecting.
discoveries.source: Government of South Australia · SA Museum
discoveries.meta_credit: Government of South Australia · SA Museum
discoveries.credit: 'Ethereal Encounter' © Matt Deakin, Australian Geographic Nature Photographer of the Year 2026

discoveries.headline: Calm and ease, with Thich Nhat Hanh
discoveries.why: One of the most loved guided meditations in the free Plum Village app: in, out, deep, slow, calm, ease. Twenty minutes, or carry the short version with you on a walk.

discoveries.headline: How gratitude rewires your brain
discoveries.why: Psychologist Christina Costa was diagnosed with a brain tumour and turned her own research on herself. Instead of fighting, she chose gratitude, and found it built more resilience. Ten minutes that change how you meet a hard week.

discoveries.headline: Lee Lai's Cannon, the first graphic novel to win the Stella
discoveries.why: Lucy Cannon cooks in a high-pressure kitchen, cares for her grandfather and watches a friendship sour. Lee Lai drew it all, and became the first cartoonist to win the $60,000 Stella Prize. Champion her: borrow it, buy it or pass it on.

discoveries.headline: Can exercise make you biologically younger?
discoveries.why: Longevity researcher Professor Andrea Maier joins Norman Swan and Dr Preeya Alexander to explain DNA tests of 'biological age', and what a big review found about moving more and ageing slower. General information, not medical advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: ABC Listen · Health Report · Prof Andrea Maier

discoveries.headline: Twenty minutes of yin, no props needed
discoveries.why: Dreena Burton's all-levels yin sequence holds each pose for a few quiet minutes, the opposite of a rushed flow. A gentle Sunday ritual for a body that has been busy all week.

discoveries.headline: Strength training, the plain-English guide
discoveries.why: Victoria's Better Health Channel on how to start: two or three sessions a week, one set of eight to begin with, building to two or three sets, and 48 hours' rest for each muscle. Stronger bones, better balance, better sleep.
